name: Civilian Complaint Review Board: Allegations Against Police Officers
description:
This dataset contains records of allegations filed against New York City police officers with the Civilian Complaint Review Board (CCRB). Each row represents a single allegation tied to a complaint, with identifiers for the complaint and the accused officer, along with the officer's rank and command at the time of the incident and how many days the officer had been on the force. It also captures the type of alleged misconduct (FADO category and specific allegation), demographic details about the alleged victim (age range, gender, race and ethnicity), the investigator's recommendation, and the final dispositions reached by the CCRB and the NYPD. A snapshot date indicates when the data was current.

The data can be used to study patterns in police misconduct allegations, such as which types of allegations are most common, how dispositions vary by allegation type or officer experience, and whether outcomes differ across victim demographics or officer ranks and commands. It supports analyses of CCRB and NYPD decision-making, research on police accountability, and public transparency dashboards
